title: Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Scam losses and reports
sections.summary: Scams often go unreported, yet reported worldwide losses grew about 16% from 2020 to over $77 billion in 2021, and Police reported over 31,000 scam cases in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Many scams go unreported, because victims feel embarrassed or do not believe any good will come of their reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But even just counting those that were reported, the amount lost to scams worldwide grew by about 16% from 2020 to over $77 billion in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Police reported that scam cases exceeded 31,000 in 2022.

sections.label: ScamShield app and blocked calls
sections.summary: Close to 60 million calls are blocked monthly, and the ScamShield app launched in November 2020 has over 550,000 downloads and filtered over 7.4 million suspected scam SMSes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Every month, close to 60 million calls are blocked.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We launched the ScamShield app in November 2020, which has been downloaded more than 550,000 times and filtered out more than 7.4 million SMSes that are suspected to be part of a scam.

sections.label: Money mules prosecuted
sections.summary: Of 19,000 money mules investigated from 2020 to 2022, fewer than 250 were prosecuted, and in the OCBC phishing scam only nine of 120 suspected money mules could be charged.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As a result of these difficulties, of the 19,000 money mules investigated by Police from 2020 to 2022, fewer than 250 money mules were eventually prosecuted.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the OCBC phishing scam which I mentioned earlier, out of the 120 suspected money mules, only nine could be charged for money mule offences.

sections.label: Rash and negligent money laundering offences
sections.summary: Clauses 3 to 6 of the CDSA Bill amend sections 50, 51, 53 and 54 to introduce offences of rash and negligent money laundering, which are not new concepts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clauses 3 to 6 of the CDSA Bill amend sections 50, 51, 53 and 54 to introduce the offences of rash and negligent money laundering. "Rash" and "negligent" are not new concepts.

sections.label: Penalties and assisting retention offence
sections.summary: Negligent money laundering carries a fine up to $150,000 or up to three years' imprisonment, or both, and clause 7 adds section 55A creating an offence of assisting another to retain benefits from criminal conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The offence of negligent money laundering will carry a fine of up to $150,000 or imprisonment of up to three years, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Based on investigations into scams, the Police have observed conduct common among money mules in facilitating a scam.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Hence, clause 7 of the Bill adds a new section 55A which introduces a new offence of assisting another person to retain benefits from criminal conduct.

sections.label: Penalty for assisting retention
sections.summary: The offence of assisting another person to retain benefits from criminal conduct carries a fine of up to $50,000 or imprisonment of up to three years, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The offence of assisting another person to retain benefits from criminal conduct will carry a fine of up to $50,000 or imprisonment of up to three years, or both.

sections.label: New Singpass credentials offence
sections.summary: Clause 4 of the CMA Bill creates a new section 8A offence covering Singpass users who deliberately give their credentials to others for criminal use.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This situation favours the scammers and it is highly unsatisfactory.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Therefore, clause 4 of the CMA Bill introduces a new offence in the form of a new section 8A in the CMA, to address the conduct of Singpass users who deliberately give their credentials to other persons, which are then used to facilitate criminal activities.

sections.label: Penalty for disclosing credentials
sections.summary: Disclosing one's own Singpass credentials carries a fine of up to $10,000 or up to three years' imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The offence of disclosing an individual's own Singpass credentials will carry a fine of up to $10,000 or imprisonment of up to three years, or both.

sections.label: Offence of dealing in credentials
sections.summary: Clause 4 also introduces section 8B, criminalising obtaining, retaining or dealing in another person's Singpass credentials.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the CMA Bill also introduces a new offence in the form of a section 8B in the CMA, which criminalises acts of obtaining, retaining or dealing in another person's Singpass credentials.

sections.label: Penalties and extraterritorial jurisdiction
sections.summary: Obtaining or dealing in Singpass credentials carries up to $10,000 or three years for a first offence, higher penalties for repeat offences, and extraterritorial court jurisdiction under clause 5.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The offence of obtaining or dealing in Singpass credentials will carry a fine of up to $10,000 or imprisonment of up to three years, or both, for a first offence.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For a second or subsequent offence, the penalty will be a fine of up to $20,000 or imprisonment of up to five years, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In addition, clause 5 amends section 13 of the CMA so that the two new offences will apply and our Courts will have jurisdiction over the offences, even if they are committed outside of Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore scam losses and cases
sections.summary: Singapore lost about $1.2 billion to scams in the last two years, with scam cases now more than 1.5 times the number of physical crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the last two years, Singapore has lost about $1.2 billion to scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Scam cases are now more than 1.5 times in number, compared to physical crimes.

sections.label: Money mule cases prosecuted
sections.summary: Between 2020 and 2022, fewer than 250 of over 19,000 money mule cases investigated were prosecuted, involving more than $440 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Currently, between 2020 and 2022, out of the more than 19,000 money mule cases investigated by the Police, only less than 250 cases were eventually prosecuted, as explained by the hon Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These cases involved amounts of more than $440 million.

sections.label: Singpass notification for vulnerable users
sections.summary: Suggests notifying next-of-kin, guardians or adult children of changes or unauthorised access to Singpass accounts of elderly and adults with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this regard, may I also suggest that for vulnerable members of our society, like the elderly and adults with special needs, that any changes or unauthorised access to their Singpass accounts also be notified to their next-of-kin, guardian or adult children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I raised in this House previously about one of my Keat Hong residents, who is an adult with special needs, and how he was scammed into signing up for various phone lines by scammers and that his elderly parents were helpless to prevent the scam.

sections.label: Two-factor authentication for Singpass changes
sections.summary: Asks what steps the Ministry will take and suggests two-factor authentication approved by next-of-kin, guardian or adult children before Singpass account access changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What are the steps that the Ministry will take to bolster such protection?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Perhaps, before any changes to access to such Singpass accounts can be made, there can be a two-factor authentication to be approved by the next-of-kin, guardian or their adult children.

sections.label: Money mule prosecution and CDSA Bill
sections.summary: Cites MHA statistics on money mules investigated and prosecuted, and states CDSA Bill clauses 3 to 6 criminalise unintentional or unknowing money laundering if rashness or negligence is shown.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) press release of 18 April 2023, a large number of money mules arrested by Police could not be prosecuted due to difficulties in proving their intent to facilitate criminal activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was highlighted that between 2020 and 2022, more than 19,000 money mules were investigated but fewer than 250 cases were eventually prosecuted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe the Second Minister stated these statistics earlier as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This works out to a prosecution rate of just 1.3%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clauses 3 to 6 of the CDSA Bill will amend sections 50, 51, 53 and 54 to criminalise acts of money laundering done unintentionally or unknowingly, if rashness or negligence can be shown.

sections.label: Defence under proposed section 55A
sections.summary: Describes a person as easily confused and cognitively impaired, and notes proposed section 55A(3) and (4) provide a defence if the person did not know or had no reasonable grounds to believe funds were proceeds of crime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: She appeared, to me at least, to be a person who was easily confused and cognitively impaired, and may have been made use of.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I note that the proposed section 55A(3) and (4) provide a defence to a charge under section 55A if the person did not know or had no reasonable grounds to believe that the funds concerned were the proceeds of crime.

sections.label: Challenges in law enforcement
sections.summary: Asks what challenges the Ministry envisages in enforcing the law and how it intends to address them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (a) What are the challenges envisaged by the Ministry with regard to enforcement of the law and how does the Ministry intend to address those challenges?

sections.label: Additional authentication levels considered
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government is considering additional authentication levels such as biometrics identification and AI-generated questions to verify identity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (c) Is the Government considering additional levels of authentication, for example, using biometrics identification, AI-generated questions, to authenticate that the individual using the identification is really who they say they are?

sections.label: COSMIC bank information sharing platform
sections.summary: The speaker says the proposed COSMIC FI-to-FI information sharing platform is pertinent because everything flows through the banking system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (d) As this inevitably always involves the banks, the proposed set-up of COSMIC, the FI-to-FI information sharing services platform, which will be debated under the amendment to the Financial Services and Markets Bill will, I believe, be pertinent because everything flows through the banking system.

sections.label: MHA involving INTERPOL counterparts
sections.summary: The question asks how MHA involves INTERPOL and overseas counterparts to ensure the Bill can be enforced effectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How does MHA involve INTERPOL and their overseas counterparts to ensure that the Bill can be enforced effectively?

sections.label: New money laundering and Singpass offences
sections.summary: The Bills introduce rash and negligent money laundering offences, expand money laundering scope, and add offences to prevent Singpass abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bills will also introduce new offences of rash and negligent money laundering, expand the scope of money laundering offences and introduce new offences to prevent Singpass abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will allow us to more effectively investigate and prosecute money mules who allow their Singpass or bank accounts to be used for scams.

sections.label: CDSA and CMA deemed liability
sections.summary: Under the CDSA Bill a person can be deemed liable for money laundering, and under the CMA Bill a person is presumed to believe disclosure was for an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act, or CDSA (Amendment) Bill, a person can be deemed liable for money laundering if they allow certain transactions to take place through their accounts without verifying the purpose of the arrangement, the source or destination of the country, or the person's identity and physical location.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the Computer Misuse Act or CMA (Amendment) Bill, a person is presumed to believe that the disclosure of his Singpass credentials was for the commission of an offence if the person fails to take steps to find out the identity and physical location of the recipient.

sections.label: Account holders responsible for transactions
sections.summary: The speaker appreciates the policy underpinning of making account holders responsible for transactions in their accounts so accounts are not used by scammers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I now turn to the proposals set out in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I appreciate the policy underpinning of the decision to make account holders responsible for the transactions in their accounts, so that their accounts would not be used by scammers.

sections.label: Concern over negligent account holder liability
sections.summary: The speaker says he should be criminally liable for helping scammers but is concerned about criminal liability for negligent account holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Hence, he should be made criminally liable for helping the scammers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I am, however, concerned about the proposal for an account holder to be criminally liable if he was negligent and that led to his account being used for money laundering activities.

sections.label: Whitewash policy for account holders
sections.summary: Proposes a policy letting account holders avoid criminal liability if they lodge a Police report soon after receiving suspected ill-gotten monies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, to have what I call a "whitewash" policy which allows for the account holders to not be held criminally liable if he were to lodge a Police report soon after they received monies which they believe to be derived from ill-gotten gains, even if they may be criminally liable in the first place for facilitating the transfer of these monies into their accounts owing to their negligence.

sections.label: Home Team account holder expectations
sections.summary: Calls for the Home Team to set out clearly in legislation or other platforms its expectations of account holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, for the Home Team to set out clearly in legislation or other platforms what its expectations of the account holders are.

sections.label: Unbanked persons and basic banking
sections.summary: Notes over 200,000 unbanked persons rejected by banks and suggests MAS and banks ensure basic banking access, even for those with criminal pasts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Government statistics show that while more than 98% of Singapore residents here have bank accounts, about 2% do not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This works out to about more than 200,000 persons here who are unbanked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As a result, the banks have assessed them to be high risk cases and rejected their applications to open bank accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I suggest that more be done between the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and banks to ensure that even if a person has a criminal past or is a subject of investigation, he or she should be able to open an account to at least to have access to basic banking services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: No bank regulated by MAS should be allowed to reject an application for basic banking services on the basis that he is high risk.

sections.label: Money mule prosecutions and evidence
sections.summary: Notes Police investigated over 19,000 money mules between 2020 and 2022 and asks whether the Bill remedies difficulty proving knowing assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Next, I note that between 2020 and 2022, the Police investigated over 19,000 money mules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Is the rate of prosecution a result of insufficient evidence?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As such, does this Bill seek to remedy the inherent difficulty of proving that money mules have knowingly assisted in money laundering offences?

sections.label: Seniors online banking scam victims
sections.summary: Asks what percentage of seniors who bank online regularly have fallen victim to scams or been involved in illegal money transfers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Amongst seniors who conduct banking activities online on a regular basis, can the Government share what percentage have fallen victim to scams or have become involved in money transfers for illegal activities?

sections.label: Bill shifts burden to accused
sections.summary: Notes the Bill eases prosecution proof by putting the onus on the accused to rebut the presumption of reasonable grounds of belief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government and relevant organisations should also continue to work towards enhancing the security of their systems to prevent the compromise of personal data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I pause here to note that the effect of the Bill makes it easier for the prosecution to prove an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In part, the Bill removes the burden on the prosecution to prove that the accused had actual knowledge or reasonable grounds to believe, and puts the onus on the accused to rebut the presumption of reasonable grounds of belief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Whilst the Bills may be contrary to the general position that one is innocent until proven otherwise, ultimately, I agree that the proposed amendments set out in the Bills are vital to meet the ever-evolving financial crimes in a digital age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Further, I firmly believe that our Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) prosecutors and our Singapore Police Force investigation officers will act judiciously in deciding whether to prosecute individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In 2022, there were 31,728 scam cases reported in Singapore, a 32.6% increase from 2021, and victims lost a staggering $660.7 million in 2022 alone, up from $632 million in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, in the last two years, $1.3 billion had been lost through scams and some of these are the retirement funds of many of our residents.

sections.label: Singpass credentials penalty
sections.summary: The proposed penalty for obtaining or dealing with Singpass credentials is a fine up to $10,000 or up to three years' imprisonment, or both, for a first offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The proposed penalty for obtaining or dealing with Singpass credentials is a maximum penalty of a fine of up to $10,000 or imprisonment of up to three years, or both, for a first offence.

sections.label: Scam victims and recovery
sections.summary: Over 53% of scam victims were aged 20 to 39, and the Anti-Scam Centre recovered over $200 million from 2019 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Contrary to popular belief, more than 53% of scam victims were between the ages of 20 and 39 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Lastly, while the amendments to the two Bills strengthen our collective defence against scams, for most scam victims, recovery of the monies lost to a scam is just as important as apprehending the scammers, if not more so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I am pleased to see in the report that over $200 million has been recovered by Anti-Scam Centre since its inception in 2019 to 2022.

sections.label: Workers' scam losses
sections.summary: Between 2021 and 2022, about $1.3 billion of workers' money was lost due to scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Over the past two years between 2021 and 2022, about $1.3 billion of workers' hard-earned money has been lost due to scams.

sections.label: Scam education and money mules
sections.summary: 53% of scam victims are 20 to 39 years old, and between 2020 and 2022 over 19,000 money mules were investigated but fewer than 250 prosecuted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: My second point is about educating the public on scam prevention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is not only the elderly that fall prey to scams, and in fact, 53% of scam victims are between 20 to 39 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In English): Mdm Deputy Speaker, with all the scam cases that are happening around us, it is unnerving to hear that between 2020 and 2022, more than 19,000 money mules were investigated by the Police, but only fewer than 250 cases were eventually prosecuted.

sections.label: Amendments to two Bills
sections.summary: The latest amendments to the two Bills seek to redress law enforcement's reach by encouraging online vigilance and responsible behaviour regarding bank accounts and Singpass details.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Yet, we cannot allow for the present situation to persist and scammers to exploit the identified loopholes in our current legal system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, the latest amendments to the two Bills have sought to redress the reach of law enforcement by encouraging online vigilance and responsible behaviour regarding the use of bank accounts and Singpass details, these are which information that was identified to have been critical in facilitating the perpetration of scams and other similar offences.

sections.label: Bank account and financial inclusion
sections.summary: Many such adults currently have no right to create a bank account, and this new amendment will only set back financial inclusion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Many such adults currently have no right to create a bank account.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This new amendment will only serve to setback the timeline for financial inclusion.

sections.label: Stakeholder involvement in scam awareness
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked about plans to involve more stakeholders, especially businesses, in scam awareness and protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: What are the Ministry's plans in involving more stakeholders, especially our businesses, in our endeavour towards scam awareness and protection?

sections.label: Bills not targeting reasonable persons
sections.summary: The Bills' provisions are not targeted at persons who had no reasonable grounds to believe they were dealing with criminal proceeds or facilitating offences.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The provisions of the Bills are not targeted at persons who had no reasonable grounds to believe they were dealing with criminal proceeds or facilitating offences.

sections.label: 2021 money mule case
sections.summary: In a 2021 case involving a 19-year-old money mule, two money mules helped launder $1 million belonging to scam victims.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In one such case which occurred in 2021, also involving a 19-year-old money mule, two money mules helped to facilitate the laundering of $1 million belonging to scam victims.

sections.label: No penalty for genuinely tricked persons
sections.summary: It is not intended to penalise those genuinely tricked into giving up bank account control or Singpass credentials, or those whose trust was betrayed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: At the same time, it is not our intention to penalise anyone who was genuinely tricked into giving up control of their bank accounts or disclosing their Singpass credentials, or those who needed help from their family members or friends and subsequently had their trust betrayed.

sections.label: Payment accounts under CDSA
sections.summary: In the CDSA, payment accounts are defined by the Payment Services Act 2019, so the new offences apply to payment accounts including e-wallets.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the CDSA, payment accounts are as defined by the Payment Services Act 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Hence, the new offences will apply to various types of payment accounts, including e-wallets.

sections.label: Goal of fewer money mules
sections.summary: The goal is not more prosecutions but far fewer money mules, and fewer prosecutions due to deterrence would be welcome.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The goal is therefore not to increase the number of prosecutions per se, but to have far fewer money mules.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: If the introduction of the new laws deters individuals from acting as money mules in the first place, resulting in fewer being prosecuted, this will be a welcome development.

sections.label: Bills commencement timing
sections.summary: The Bills, if passed, are intended to come into force about six months later so the public can familiarise themselves with the new laws.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: If passed, the Bills are intended to come into force approximately six months later to allow time for members of the public to familiarise themselves with the new laws.

sections.label: Presumption of innocence upheld
sections.summary: Both the CDSA and the CMA Bills continue to uphold and are consistent with the presumption of innocence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Both the CDSA and the CMA Bills continue to uphold and are consistent with the presumption of innocence.

sections.label: Singpass scam verification measures
sections.summary: Higher risk transactions may require Singpass Face Verification, letting GovTech act on scams, and users can block overseas Singpass access.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For higher risk transactions, users may also be asked to further verify themselves with Singpass Face Verification.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: These measures allow GovTech to take prompt action to investigate and, where possible, prevent or stop the scams.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: GovTech has also given users the option to block their Singpass from overseas access.

sections.label: Amendments against scams
sections.summary: The proposed amendments aim to build collective defence against scams, disrupt syndicates and protect Singaporeans, preserving confidence in going digital.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will build up our collective defence against scams, disrupt scam syndicates and better protect Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: If we are able to do so, it will help preserve Singaporeans' confidence in going digital, even for the elderly and more vulnerable.

sections.label: Due diligence and Police response
sections.summary: The speaker asks about due diligence measures akin to the Immigration Act, and says Police will consider negligence and harm in deciding further action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: And in relation to my suggestion that the Ministry consider putting up due diligence measures that account holders should generally subscribe to, something akin to the Immigration Act, I wonder whether the hon Second Minister has the response to that?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And indeed, the Police will look at the situation, understand where the person who made the report was coming from, examine the circumstances carefully and if indeed, it was a matter of negligence and perhaps not much harm had been done, the Police will certainly take these into consideration in deciding whether or not to proceed with further action.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In principle, we would like to get to a point where these due diligence steps can be very clearly articulated and all of us can take part in preventing scams from happening.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: At present, it would be very hard to say that "here are the three things you can do", and you would have been considered to have fulfilled your due diligence.

sections.label: Considering suggestions taken forward
sections.summary: If that situation is reached, the speaker assures willingness to consider the suggestions being taken forward.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If and when we are able to get to that situation, please be assured that we would be very willing to consider his suggestions being taken forward.      .
